title: APT28 Got Exposed by Their Own OPSEC Mistake - But Still Compromised 280+ Targets. What Does That Say?
clean_text: A pretty significant cyber espionage operation just got exposed and interestingly, it happened because the attackers made a mistake. Summary: • 280+ email accounts compromised • Campaign ran from Sept 2024 to March 2026 • Attributed to APT28 (FancyBear / GRU-linked) • Discovered after attackers exposed their own server logs Targets included: • Ukrainian prosecutors and anti-corruption agencies • Romanian Air Force (67 accounts) • Greek defense staff (28 accounts) • Local governments across Eastern Europe Why this matters: • Focused on intelligence gathering around anti-corruption and defense • Shows continued targeting of NATO-aligned regions • Coincides with increased attacks on healthcare and municipal systems Interesting angle: Even advanced APT groups can slip up operationally - but the campaign still ran for nearly two years before being exposed. Discussion points for community: How do you detect long-term, low-noise espionage campaigns? Are current email security controls enough against APT-level threats? Does OPSEC failure remain one of the biggest weak points for attackers? Curious to hear thoughts from others in the field.
